skill.name: agentdb-performance-optimization
skill.description: Optimize AgentDB vector database performance with quantization, HNSW indexing, caching, batch operations, and monitoring guidance.
skill.summary: Tune AgentDB search speed, memory use, and scaling strategy for vector workloads.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Static findings for Ruby backtick execution, hardcoded URLs, and SQLite paths are false positives from Markdown documentation examples. I found one semantic risk: the guide recommends unpinned npx commands that can fetch package code that changes over time. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious data-access intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unpinned npx package execution in benchmark and stats examples
remediation.suggestion: Pin the agentdb package version, document the expected package source, and require explicit user confirmation before running npx commands.

remediation.issue: Command examples can be interpreted as agent actions
remediation.suggestion: Label shell commands as optional manual steps and include a dry-run or inspection step before execution.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned External Package Execution Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The guide instructs users or agents to run npx commands with @latest. Running a latest package can fetch and execute code that changes over time, so it should require version pinning and user confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The bash examples use npx with @latest, which is a concrete supply-chain execution risk if an agent runs them automatically. The intent appears to be legitimate benchmarking, so medium severity is appropriate.

content.value_statement: Large AgentDB vector stores can become slow and memory heavy as data grows. This skill gives quantization, HNSW, caching, and batching guidance for faster search and lower memory use.
actual_capabilities: Explains binary, scalar, product, and full-precision quantization choices.
Shows AgentDB adapter settings for HNSW, cache size, and quantization.
Provides benchmark commands for AgentDB search, insert, and memory metrics.
Describes batch retrieval and insert patterns for vector workloads.
Offers scaling recipes for small through million-vector databases.
Includes troubleshooting steps for memory, speed, and accuracy issues.
limitations: It is guidance only; it does not run benchmarks or modify databases by itself.
Published benchmark numbers depend on hardware, data, and AgentDB version.
Some commands rely on npm package execution and should be reviewed before running.
It does not verify application-specific recall, latency, or data quality targets.

use_cases.title: Tune Production Vector Search
use_cases.description: Choose AgentDB quantization, HNSW, and cache settings for a growing search service.

use_cases.title: Reduce Memory Footprint
use_cases.description: Plan compression and pruning changes before deploying AgentDB on constrained infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Compare Scaling Options
use_cases.description: Estimate speed, accuracy, and memory tradeoffs before moving to larger embedding collections.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Quantization Mode
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new AgentDB project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an AgentDB quantization mode for my dataset size, memory limit, and accuracy target.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Search Latency
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AgentDB search latency goals and recommend HNSW, cache, and retrieval settings to test first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Scaling Upgrade
prompt_templates.scenario: Preparing for a larger vector collection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an AgentDB scaling plan for moving from my current vector count to my target count while controlling memory use.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Benchmark Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a benchmark and risk review for AgentDB performance changes, including recall checks, latency targets, and command safety.

output_examples.input: I have 500,000 document embeddings and memory usage is too high.
output: Recommended path: test binary quantization if a small recall loss is acceptable.
Validation step: compare recall against a representative query set before rollout.
Operational check: monitor database size, cache hit rate, and average search latency.

output_examples.input: Search is slow on a medium AgentDB collection.
output: Start with scalar quantization, a moderate cache, and balanced HNSW search quality.
Measure latency before and after each change so improvements are attributable.
Avoid lowering search quality until recall requirements are clearly defined.

output_examples.input: We need a safe benchmark plan for AgentDB optimization.
output: Use a copied database or staging environment for benchmarks.
Pin any external package versions before command execution.
Record hardware, data size, latency, memory, and recall results together.

best_practices: Benchmark current latency, recall, and memory before changing optimization settings.
Pin package versions and review commands before running benchmarks in a real workspace.
Validate accuracy after quantization with representative production queries.
anti_patterns: Do not choose binary quantization for accuracy-critical workloads without recall testing.
Do not increase cache size without checking memory limits.
Do not run latest-package commands automatically in sensitive environments.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my AgentDB database?
faq.answer: No. It provides optimization guidance and examples. Any database changes require separate user action.

faq.question: Which AgentDB optimization should I try first?
faq.answer: Start with measurement, then test cache size and scalar quantization before more aggressive compression.

faq.question: Can binary quantization reduce accuracy?
faq.answer: Yes. Binary quantization can reduce recall, so validate results with representative queries.

faq.question: Are the benchmark numbers guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on hardware, data distribution, vector dimensions, and AgentDB version.

faq.question: Is it safe to run the listed npx commands?
faq.answer: Review them first, pin package versions, and run them only in trusted environments.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
